title: Cell theory, scale, and emergence mastery check

items.prompt: An observer holds a specimen at 40 cm and has the standard angular resolution limit of 1 minute of arc, which is about 2.9 x 10^-4 radians. The cells in the specimen are 12 µm across. Work out the smallest separation the observer can resolve at that distance, give the factor by which a cell falls short of it, and state whether the observer could establish that the specimen is built from separate units. Then say what a conventional light microscope, with a lateral limit of about 0.25 µm, would add, giving the factor there as well. Show the arithmetic and carry the units through it.

answer.correct: At 40 cm the smallest resolvable separation is s = d x theta = 400 mm x 2.9 x 10^-4 = 0.116 mm, which is about 116 µm. A 12 µm cell is smaller than that by a factor of 116/12, which is about 10, so the observer cannot resolve one cell from the next and cannot establish that the specimen is built from separate units, however carefully they look. A conventional light microscope with a lateral limit of about 0.25 µm sits below the cell width by a factor of 12/0.25, which is about 48, so it separates neighbouring cells with a wide margin and settles the question that the unaided eye cannot even address.
answer.summary: About 116 µm at 40 cm, a cell roughly ten times smaller than that, so no; a light microscope has about forty-eight times the margin needed, so yes.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for the conversion, which requires the distance in a length unit and the angle in radians and yields about 116 µm; a response that reports 0.1 mm as a remembered constant rather than computing it at 40 cm does not earn this point, because the whole content of the relation is that the threshold moves with distance. Award one point for the factor of about ten and the correct verdict that the cell is below the threshold. Award one point for the light-microscope comparison with its factor of about forty-eight and the statement that the instrument therefore resolves the cells. On a retry, run the same three steps for an observer at 20 cm looking at 18 µm cells, which gives a threshold near 58 µm and a factor near 3, and note that the verdict does not change even though both numbers do.
acceptableResponses: Any response that multiplies the distance by the angle with consistent units to obtain roughly 0.1 mm at 40 cm, gives a factor near ten against a 12 µm cell with the correct negative verdict, and gives a factor near fifty for the light microscope with the correct positive verdict. Values within about twenty per cent of these figures are correct, since the inputs are themselves approximate.
commonErrors: Quoting 100 µm from the lesson instead of computing the threshold at the stated 40 cm
Multiplying by the angle in degrees or arcminutes rather than radians
Reporting the threshold in millimetres and the cell in micrometres and then dividing without converting
Concluding that a light microscope cannot help because the cell is smaller than the eye's threshold
Giving the verdict with no factor, so nothing shows how far short the cell falls

items.prompt: A classmate writes: "Cell theory is only a theory, so the whole of histology rests on an assumption nobody has checked." Write a reply of a few sentences. State what cell theory asserts, including the boundary on how new cells arise. For two of its propositions, name an observation that would count strongly against it and say whether anyone was in a position to look. Then explain what a scientific theory is, how it differs from a hypothesis, and how both differ from the everyday sense your classmate is using.

answer.correct: Cell theory asserts that tissues of plants and animals are composed of cells as their basic unit and that cells continue pre-existing cellular lineages rather than appearing from non-cellular material. Division is the usual route, but not a universal one: a skeletal muscle fibre forms when pre-existing myoblasts fuse. The composition claim would be seriously challenged by a reproducible tissue built from something other than cells, and microscopy across plants, animals, and human organs repeatedly tested that scope. The lineage claim would be seriously challenged by a reproducible cell origin with no pre-existing cellular material; nineteenth-century proposals of formation from non-cellular material were investigated and did not survive. A scientific theory is a broad, coherent and predictive explanatory framework that integrates observations and hypotheses, remains revisable, and earns confidence from the evidence supporting it. A hypothesis is a more specific proposition that evidence can evaluate and that may test or extend a theory; it is not a lower rung that automatically becomes a theory. The everyday sense of theory as an untested private guess is different. Histology relies on cell theory as a well-supported framework, not as an unchecked assumption.
answer.summary: The composition and cellular-lineage propositions with the division-versus-fusion boundary, two observations that would count against them, and a distinction among a broad revisable theory, a testable hypothesis, and an everyday guess.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for a statement of what cell theory asserts that includes both the composition claim and continuity from pre-existing cells or cellular lineages, and that does not require every specialised cell to form by division. Award one point for two propositions each paired with a concrete observation that would count strongly against it, together with some indication that the question was actually pursued; naming the propositions without an evidentiary test does not earn this point. Award one point for describing a theory as a broad, evidence-supported and revisable explanation, distinguishing it from a more specific hypothesis without a promotion ladder, and answering the classmate's conclusion about histology. On a retry, use the same structure for germ theory: its scope, evidence that would challenge it, the role of a narrower hypothesis, and why the everyday word guess does not describe the framework.
acceptableResponses: Any reply that states the composition and cellular-lineage assertions with a scientifically valid qualification on division, supplies a challenging observation for two propositions with evidence that the questions were pursued, and distinguishes a broad evidence-supported and revisable theory from both a more specific hypothesis and an everyday guess.
commonErrors: Answering that a hypothesis automatically becomes a theory after enough support, which treats the terms as consecutive rungs rather than different explanatory roles
Asserting that cell theory has been proved, which claims more than any evidence supplies
Requiring every living or specialised cell to divide, or saying that every cell forms directly by one cell division
Listing the propositions with no observation that could have refuted any of them
Correcting the vocabulary while leaving the classmate's claim about histology unanswered
Treating popularity or textbook status as the reason the account is trusted

items.prompt: Along a colonic crypt, signalling from the base falls off with height, so how much signal a cell receives carries information about how far up the crypt it has travelled. Which statement classifies that gradient correctly, and for the right reason?

options.text: Not emergent, because each cell has its own receptors and therefore carries the property itself.
Emergent, because a gradient is a difference across an arranged population, so a cell taken out of the crypt has no position left for a gradient to encode.
Emergent, because a crypt contains about 700 cells and a single cell contains one.
Not emergent, because every step in the crypt reduces to ordinary chemistry and physics.

answer.summary: Emergent in this lesson's bounded tissue-level sense, because position is a relation across an arranged population and a dissociated cell has none.
answer.reasoning: Both parts of the lesson's operational test point the same way. Look for the property in one cell and you find receptors and a response to a signal, which is a different property from a difference in signal across a population. Disrupt the crypt arrangement while keeping every cell alive and the positional gradient goes even though every cell is intact. The receptor option finds a related property in a component and stops there. The option about 700 cells names number instead of arrangement; 700 cells shaken into a tube have no gradient at all. The chemistry option treats emergence as a claim that something non-physical has been added, which this bounded use explicitly denies: interacting components and their spatial arrangement are doing the work. The item tests the stated epithelial convention, not every technical meaning of emergence. On a retry, classify two more: the mucus layer covering the epithelium, and a single cell's ability to manufacture a mucin protein.
commonErrors: Locating a related single-cell property and treating it as the property in question
Using the number of cells rather than their arrangement as the reason
Reading emergence as a claim that something non-physical has been added
Applying only the first half of the test and skipping the dissociation check

items.prompt: An invented research team drafts a protocol to watch colonic crypt renewal. Their imaging system delivers about 40 µm of resolution to the observer and can run continuously for six hours. The draft states three things they intend to report. First, the mean diameter of the crypt cells, to one decimal place. Second, continuous tissue-level exclusion of luminal contents across an area as a property of each individual cell. Third, that cell theory says every cell in every tissue forms directly by one cell division, so that proposition is untestable and will not be examined. Judge each of the three. Then, working only within the lesson's idealised scale-and-diffraction model, state the resolution and observation time needed to follow one cell from the base of a crypt to the surface, explain each number, and state what the model cannot establish about real feasibility. No real study, device, patient, or clinical procedure is described here, and nothing in this item is guidance for any real investigation.

answer.correct: For a surface view, crypt depth is irrelevant. In the lesson's simplified circular model, 22 cells of about 10 µm around a perimeter imply an opening about 70 µm across, so 40 µm reaches the scale of one opening. The model gives no opening-to-opening separation, however, so it cannot establish that neighbouring openings, their spacing, or their density are resolved. A 10 to 20 µm cell is finer than 40 µm and is not resolved. The first report therefore fails twice: the instrument cannot separate one cell from its neighbour, and a diameter to one decimal place claims precision the stipulated method cannot supply. The second report assigns a tissue-level predicate to one component. An individual epithelial cell has transcellular transport and permeability properties, and the junctions between cells regulate paracellular permeability, but continuous exclusion across an area belongs to the joined sheet and is lost when that arrangement is disrupted. The third report is wrong in two ways. Cell theory preserves cellular lineage, but division is not the direct formation route for every specialised cell: multinucleate skeletal muscle fibres form by fusion of pre-existing myoblasts. The framework also remains testable and revisable; a reproducible cell origin without pre-existing cellular material would count strongly against the lineage principle. Within the idealised model, following one crypt cell requires resolution finer than about 10 µm and observation for roughly three to seven days under the constant-speed assumption. The conventional light-microscope floor near 0.25 µm shows only that diffraction is not the limiting term in that numerical comparison. The model supplies no evidence about optical access, contrast or labelling, tissue effects, motion, safety, or tracking stability, so it cannot establish that engineering is the only obstacle or that the real observation is feasible.
answer.summary: A modelled opening-scale comparison that does not establish spacing, one impossible and falsely precise cell measurement, a bounded tissue-level barrier predicate, a qualified cellular-lineage principle that remains testable, and an idealised redesign needing sub-10 µm resolution and several days without claiming real feasibility.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for a dimensionally valid resolution analysis: the 40 µm system reaches the modelled opening diameter near 70 µm but the supplied data do not establish opening-to-opening spacing or density, while cells of 10 to 20 µm remain unresolved. Award one point for rejecting the first report on both resolution and false-precision grounds. Award one point for classifying continuous tissue-level exclusion as emergent in the lesson's bounded sense while preserving the individual cell's transcellular permeability and the junction-dependent paracellular route. Award one point for correcting both errors in the third report and completing the bounded redesign: cellular lineage does not require every specialised cell to form by one division, the proposition remains open to evidence, and the model requires resolution below one cell width for roughly three to seven days under its stated migration assumption but cannot establish real feasibility or reduce all other constraints to engineering. On a retry, review a second invented protocol: an instrument delivering 8 µm of resolution that runs for a week but images only a single fixed plane through the tissue.
acceptableResponses: Any response that compares 40 µm with the modelled opening diameter and the cell width without inferring opening spacing or density, rejects the decimal-place measurement on resolution and precision grounds, distinguishes continuous tissue-level exclusion from transcellular and paracellular permeability, qualifies the cellular-lineage principle and its testability, gives sub-10 µm and multi-day requirements within the idealised model, and states that those numbers do not establish real feasibility.
commonErrors: Rejecting all three reports without separating the instrument error from the category error from the vocabulary error
Rejecting the cell-diameter report only because the instrument is too coarse, leaving the false precision unremarked
Denying all permeability properties of an individual epithelial cell instead of distinguishing transcellular, paracellular, and continuous tissue-level properties
Repeating the historical division formula as an exceptionless rule for every specialised cell
Agreeing that a well-established proposition is untestable
Giving a resolution requirement and forgetting that the observation must run for days
Concluding that engineering is the only real obstacle merely because the conventional diffraction floor is below the stipulated requirement

rubrics.title: Computing a resolution threshold and comparing it with a cell

criteria.description: Award 1 point only when the threshold is computed from the stated 40 cm distance and the angle in radians, giving about 116 µm, with units carried through. A remembered 0.1 mm does not earn it.
Award 1 point only when the cell is compared with that threshold as a factor of about ten and the verdict is that an unaided observer cannot establish separate units.
Award 1 point only when the light microscope's 0.25 µm limit is compared with the 12 µm cell as a factor of about forty-eight and the correct positive verdict follows.

rubrics.title: Defending the standing of cell theory

criteria.description: Award 1 point only when the reply states both that tissues are composed of cells and that cells continue pre-existing cellular lineages, without requiring every specialised cell to form by one cell division.
Award 1 point only when two propositions each carry a concrete reproducible observation that would count strongly against them, together with an indication that the question was actually pursued.

Award 1 point only when a broad, evidence-supported and revisable theory is distinguished from a more specific hypothesis without a promotion ladder, the everyday sense of guess is separated, and the conclusion about histology is answered.

rubrics.title: Classifying a crypt property as emergent

criteria.description: Award 2 points only when the arranged-population option is selected; that option contains both the bounded tissue-level classification and the decisive reason that positional information is lost when the crypt arrangement is disrupted.

rubrics.title: Integrated review of an unfamiliar observation protocol

criteria.description: Award 1 point only when 40 µm is compared with the modelled opening diameter near 70 µm and the 10 to 20 µm cell width, with the explicit boundary that no opening-to-opening spacing or density can be inferred from the supplied dimensions.
Award 1 point only when the cell-diameter report is rejected on both grounds, the instrument's inability to separate cells and the precision the method cannot produce.
Award 1 point only when continuous tissue-level exclusion is classified as emergent while individual-cell transcellular permeability and junction-dependent paracellular permeability are preserved.

Award 1 point only when the universal direct-division claim and the word untestable are both corrected, and the idealised redesign supplies sub-cell-width resolution and a multi-day observation while stating that those numbers do not establish real feasibility.
